Information since September points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, but with notable headwinds from weak business fixed investment and exports alongside inflation running below 2%. The 25 bp cut to 1.50–1.75% and the Desk’s bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves are consistent with the literature showing that monetary policy supports real activity and price stability (e.g., Sims’ VAR evidence; B. Friedman). The emphasis on soft capex aligns with findings that investment is highly sensitive to internal funds/credit conditions and often drives GDP slowdowns (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994; investment spending’s outsized role in downturns). With survey- and market-based inflation expectations stable, New Keynesian estimates of the Phillips curve (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) suggest subdued inflation is consistent with a modest output gap, reinforcing the case for precautionary easing. Open-economy models also imply that easing can support net exports via a more competitive real exchange rate, partially offsetting external weakness. Net tone: mildly positive but cautious.
